##HEADER W11 · Ensemble data assimilation of fault stress (boundary case). R3 · physical · random · SAME · compute_tested: yes · expected: if_not
##QUESTION On a fault whose physics we control, does earthquake-forecast skill keep rising as the ensemble grows (compute)? Or does it level off early, while model error and sensor depth decide the outcome?
##PRIOR van Dinther et al. 2019: a 150-member EnKF on a 2-D lab-scale subduction model, perfect model; "as little as 20 ensemble members" captured most of the diversity [s3]. Left open: none of the sources reviewed reports forecast skill as a function of ensemble size beyond 150 members, none under deliberate model error on a depth-resolved rate-and-state fault, none compares an EnKF with a large particle filter on the same fault. Search: unavailable.
##HYPOTHESIS Skill levels off at tens to hundreds of members, which would confirm W11 with a measured curve in place of an argument.
##IF_LEVER In E2 or E4, ASS is still rising beyond M = 1,024 by more than the E3 gain from deep data. In that case, in this synthetic world, buying ensemble members beats buying sensors.
##IF_NOT M* ≤ 256 in every EnKF arm (E1, E2), and the skill lost to model error (E2), or gained from a stress sensor at depth (E3), is larger than the skill gained by going from M = 32 to the largest M.
##RULE ASS(M) is the area skill score for full ruptures, averaged over the 5 truths, with its standard error across truths. M* is the smallest M whose ASS is within one standard error of the ASS at the largest M.
##AXIS Ensemble size M (members): 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1,024, 4,096 (EnKF); 1,024, 4,096, 16,384 (PF). Held fixed: truth regime, observation network, alarm rule. Closest prior: 150 [s3].
##ANCHOR BP1, one member, 25 m cells: recurrence interval and first-event time within 1% of QDYN [s7].
##LIMITS Even the second outcome would only show that compute matters when the model class is known. It says nothing about observing a real fault's stress (C2), which is what W11's verdict rests on. The noise is badly tuned: too little and the pattern-repeat baseline wins; too much and the noise swamps the physics.
##COST $684 planned of $1,000: 6 h on 1× H100 ($25.74), 20 h on 8× H100 at $31.92/h ($638.40), storage up to $20 (GUESS). Two GPU timings are GUESS; the $25.74 phase measures them. Not bought: the same runs without active-set compaction, $6,120.
